items.title: Glueing invertible sheaves and compatible nonvanishing sections from closed subschemes meeting in a discrete set
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section on glueing invertible sheaves

items.difficulty_reason: The lemma glues invertible sheaves L_i on closed subschemes Z_i covering a reduced scheme X, assuming the pairwise intersections are discrete, and additionally glues sections s_i that are nonvanishing at the points of the intersections. The proof must first note that X minus T is the disjoint union of the Z_i minus T for the discrete set T of pairwise intersections, then choose separating opens U_t around each point of T together with trivializations, cover each Z_i minus T by opens, and build the cocycle data for the glued sheaf (proof lines 8012-8067). The section half of the proof requires keeping track of the chosen trivializations so that the local sections agree on overlaps (proof lines 8021 onwards). H3: the construction of the cocycle and the simultaneous control of the sections is an independent research-level argument, not a routine application of descent.
